_comment: Hand-hardened profile for the engine itself (issue #4), in the OCI/Docker profile format.
Default action is KILL_PROCESS, so this is an exact allowlist: the parent survives only if the enumeration in baseline/ is complete.

Group 1: the engine's start-up set from baseline/*.txt. poll and arch_prctl are the x86_64 counterparts of ppoll and musl TLS setup; prctl is the engine's init setting PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 (RLIMIT_CORE does not stop piped cores).

Group 2: the isolation harness (#5-#7): clone (musl's fork) for the child, pidfd_open, ppoll on the pidfd (group 1) for the bounded wait, wait4, close of the pidfd, kill on timeout, write for output, exit_group. clone3/waitid/exit/rt_sigreturn are not issued today and are kept for a future harness change.

Group 3: runc's own pre-exec set. runc applies this filter and then still issues these before execve, so a profile without them kills runc init, not the engine. Found on runc 1.5.1 by running --noop under KILL_PROCESS and adding the audited syscall until runc reached execve, on aarch64 (27) and x86_64 (+clock_gettime: Go's vDSO clock falls back to the syscall when the clocksource is not vDSO-capable, as under emulation, so whether runc needs it is a property of the node). Every kill was comm=runc:[2:INIT], none was the engine. runc also issues close and prctl, listed in groups 2 and 1. A property of the runtime, not of the engine: the seccompiler test in crates/probe/tests applies groups 1-2 alone at execve.
